__global__
void allenCahn(double phinew[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
               double phiold[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
               double uold[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
               double Fx[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
               double Fy[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
               double Fz[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
               double epsilon, double W0, double tau0, double lambda,
               double dt, double dx, double dy, double dz)
{
  unsigned iz = blockIdx.x*blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
  unsigned iy = blockIdx.y*blockDim.y + threadIdx.y;
  unsigned ix = blockIdx.z*blockDim.z + threadIdx.z;

  if ((ix < (DATAXSIZE-1)) && (iy < (DATAYSIZE-1)) &&
      (iz < (DATAZSIZE-1)) && (ix > (0)) &&

    double phix = GradientX(phiold,dx,dy,dz,ix,iy,iz);
    double phiy = GradientY(phiold,dx,dy,dz,ix,iy,iz);

          u[idx][idy][idz] = 0.0;
        }

      }

int main(int argc, char *argv[])
{
  const int num_steps = atoi(argv[1]);  //6000;
  const double dx = 0.4;
  const double dy = 0.4;
  const double dz = 0.4;
  const double dt = 0.01;
  const double delta = 0.8;
  const double r0 = 5.0;
  const double epsilon = 0.07;
  const double W0 = 1.0;
  const double beta0 = 0.0;
  const double D = 2.0;
  const double d0 = 0.5;
  const double a1 = 1.25 / std::sqrt(2.0);
  const double a2 = 0.64;
  const double lambda = (W0*a1)/(d0);
  const double tau0 = ((W0*W0*W0*a1*a2)/(d0*D)) + ((W0*W0*beta0)/(d0));

  // overall data set sizes
  const int nx = DATAXSIZE;
  const int ny = DATAYSIZE;
  const int nz = DATAZSIZE;
  const int vol = nx * ny * nz;
  const size_t vol_in_bytes = sizeof(double) * vol;

  // pointers for data set storage via malloc
  nRarray *phi_host;
  nRarray *d_phiold;
  nRarray *u_host;
  nRarray *d_phinew;
  nRarray *d_uold;
  nRarray *d_unew;
  nRarray *d_Fx;
  nRarray *d_Fy;
  nRarray *d_Fz;

  phi_host = (nRarray *)malloc(vol_in_bytes);
  u_host = (nRarray *)malloc(vol_in_bytes);

  initializationPhi(phi_host,r0);
  initializationU(u_host,r0,delta);

#ifdef VERIFY
  nRarray *phi_ref = (nRarray *)malloc(vol_in_bytes);
  nRarray *u_ref = (nRarray *)malloc(vol_in_bytes);
  memcpy(phi_ref, phi_host, vol_in_bytes);
  memcpy(u_ref, u_host, vol_in_bytes);
  reference(phi_ref, u_ref, vol, num_steps);
#endif

  auto offload_start = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();

  // define the chunk sizes that each threadblock will work on
  dim3 grid ((DATAZSIZE+7)/8, (DATAYSIZE+7)/8, (DATAXSIZE+3)/4);
  dim3 block (8, 8, 4);

  // allocate GPU device buffers
  cudaMalloc((void **) &d_phiold, vol_in_bytes);
  cudaMalloc((void **) &d_phinew, vol_in_bytes);
  cudaMalloc((void **) &d_uold, vol_in_bytes);
  cudaMalloc((void **) &d_unew, vol_in_bytes);
  cudaMalloc((void **) &d_Fx, vol_in_bytes);
  cudaMalloc((void **) &d_Fy, vol_in_bytes);
  cudaMalloc((void **) &d_Fz, vol_in_bytes);

  cudaMemcpy(d_phiold, phi_host, vol_in_bytes, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice);
  cudaMemcpy(d_uold, u_host, vol_in_bytes, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice);

  int t = 0;

  cudaDeviceSynchronize();
  auto start = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();

  while (t <= num_steps) {

    calculateForce<<<grid, block>>>(d_phiold,d_Fx,d_Fy,d_Fz,
                                    dx,dy,dz,epsilon,W0,tau0);

    allenCahn<<<grid, block>>>(d_phinew,d_phiold,d_uold,
                               d_Fx,d_Fy,d_Fz,
                               epsilon,W0,tau0,lambda,
                               dt,dx,dy,dz);

    boundaryConditionsPhi<<<grid, block>>>(d_phinew);

    thermalEquation<<<grid, block>>>(d_unew,d_uold,d_phinew,d_phiold,
                                     D,dt,dx,dy,dz);

    boundaryConditionsU<<<grid, block>>>(d_unew,delta);

    swapGrid<<<grid, block>>>(d_phinew, d_phiold);

    swapGrid<<<grid, block>>>(d_unew, d_uold);

    t++;
  }

  cudaDeviceSynchronize();
  auto end = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
  auto time = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::nanoseconds>(end - start).count();
  printf("Total kernel execution time: %.3f (ms)\n", time * 1e-6f);

  cudaMemcpy(phi_host, d_phiold, vol_in_bytes, cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost);
  cudaMemcpy(u_host, d_uold, vol_in_bytes, cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost);

  cudaFree(d_phiold);
  cudaFree(d_phinew);
  cudaFree(d_uold);
  cudaFree(d_unew);
  cudaFree(d_Fx);
  cudaFree(d_Fy);
  cudaFree(d_Fz);

  auto offload_end = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
  auto offload_time = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::nanoseconds>(offload_end - offload_start).count();
  printf("Offload time: %.3f (ms)\n", offload_time * 1e-6f);

#ifdef VERIFY
  bool ok = true;
  for (int idx = 0; idx < nx; idx++)
    for (int idy = 0; idy < ny; idy++)
      for (int idz = 0; idz < nz; idz++) {
        if (fabs(phi_ref[idx][idy][idz] - phi_host[idx][idy][idz]) > 1e-3) {
          ok = false; printf("phi: %lf %lf\n", phi_ref[idx][idy][idz], phi_host[idx][idy][idz]);
	}
        if (fabs(u_ref[idx][idy][idz] - u_host[idx][idy][idz]) > 1e-3) {
          ok = false; printf("u: %lf %lf\n", u_ref[idx][idy][idz], u_host[idx][idy][idz]);
        }
      }
  printf("%s\n", ok ? "PASS" : "FAIL");
  free(phi_ref);
  free(u_ref);
#endif

  free(phi_host);
  free(u_host);
  return 0;
}

#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <math.h>
#include <chrono>
#include <cuda.h>

//define the data set size (cubic volume)
#define DATAXSIZE 400
#define DATAYSIZE 400
#define DATAZSIZE 400

typedef double nRarray[DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE];

// square
#define SQ(x) ((x)*(x))

#ifdef VERIFY
#include <string.h>
#include "reference.h"
#endif

__device__
double dFphi(double phi, double u, double lambda)
{
  return (-phi*(1.0-phi*phi)+lambda*u*(1.0-phi*phi)*(1.0-phi*phi));
}

__device__
double GradientX(double phi[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
                 double dx, double dy, double dz, int x, int y, int z)
{
  return (phi[x+1][y][z] - phi[x-1][y][z]) / (2.0*dx);
}

__device__
double GradientY(double phi[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
                 double dx, double dy, double dz, int x, int y, int z)
{
  return (phi[x][y+1][z] - phi[x][y-1][z]) / (2.0*dy);
}

__device__
double GradientZ(double phi[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
                 double dx, double dy, double dz, int x, int y, int z)
{
  return (phi[x][y][z+1] - phi[x][y][z-1]) / (2.0*dz);
}

__device__
double Divergence(double phix[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
                  double phiy[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
                  double phiz[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
                  double dx, double dy, double dz, int x, int y, int z)
{
  return GradientX(phix,dx,dy,dz,x,y,z) +
         GradientY(phiy,dx,dy,dz,x,y,z) +
         GradientZ(phiz,dx,dy,dz,x,y,z);
}

__device__
double Laplacian(double phi[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
                 double dx, double dy, double dz, int x, int y, int z)
{
  double phixx = (phi[x+1][y][z] + phi[x-1][y][z] - 2.0 * phi[x][y][z]) / SQ(dx);
  double phiyy = (phi[x][y+1][z] + phi[x][y-1][z] - 2.0 * phi[x][y][z]) / SQ(dy);
  double phizz = (phi[x][y][z+1] + phi[x][y][z-1] - 2.0 * phi[x][y][z]) / SQ(dz);
  return phixx + phiyy + phizz;
}

__device__
double An(double phix, double phiy, double phiz, double epsilon)
{
  if (phix != 0.0 || phiy != 0.0 || phiz != 0.0){
    return ((1.0 - 3.0 * epsilon) * (1.0 + (((4.0 * epsilon) / (1.0-3.0*epsilon))*
           ((SQ(phix)*SQ(phix)+SQ(phiy)*SQ(phiy)+SQ(phiz)*SQ(phiz)) /
           ((SQ(phix)+SQ(phiy)+SQ(phiz))*(SQ(phix)+SQ(phiy)+SQ(phiz)))))));
  }
  else
  {
    return (1.0-((5.0/3.0)*epsilon));
  }
}

__device__
double Wn(double phix, double phiy, double phiz, double epsilon, double W0)
{
  return (W0*An(phix,phiy,phiz,epsilon));
}

__device__
double taun(double phix, double phiy, double phiz, double epsilon, double tau0)
{
  return tau0 * SQ(An(phix,phiy,phiz,epsilon));
}

__device__
double dFunc(double l, double m, double n)
{
  if (l != 0.0 || m != 0.0 || n != 0.0){
    return (((l*l*l*(SQ(m)+SQ(n)))-(l*(SQ(m)*SQ(m)+SQ(n)*SQ(n)))) /
            ((SQ(l)+SQ(m)+SQ(n))*(SQ(l)+SQ(m)+SQ(n))));
  }
  else
  {
    return 0.0;
  }
}

__global__
void calculateForce(double phi[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
                    double Fx[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
                    double Fy[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
                    double Fz[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
                    double dx, double dy, double dz,
                    double epsilon, double W0, double tau0)
{

  unsigned iz = blockIdx.x*blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
  unsigned iy = blockIdx.y*blockDim.y + threadIdx.y;
  unsigned ix = blockIdx.z*blockDim.z + threadIdx.z;

  if ((ix < (DATAXSIZE-1)) && (iy < (DATAYSIZE-1)) &&
      (iz < (DATAZSIZE-1)) && (ix > (0)) &&
      (iy > (0)) && (iz > (0))) {

    double phix = GradientX(phi,dx,dy,dz,ix,iy,iz);
    double phiy = GradientY(phi,dx,dy,dz,ix,iy,iz);
    double phiz = GradientZ(phi,dx,dy,dz,ix,iy,iz);
    double sqGphi = SQ(phix) + SQ(phiy) + SQ(phiz);
    double c = 16.0 * W0 * epsilon;
    double w = Wn(phix,phiy,phiz,epsilon,W0);
    double w2 = SQ(w);


    Fx[ix][iy][iz] = w2 * phix + sqGphi * w * c * dFunc(phix,phiy,phiz);
    Fy[ix][iy][iz] = w2 * phiy + sqGphi * w * c * dFunc(phiy,phiz,phix);
    Fz[ix][iy][iz] = w2 * phiz + sqGphi * w * c * dFunc(phiz,phix,phiy);
  }
  else
  {
    Fx[ix][iy][iz] = 0.0;
    Fy[ix][iy][iz] = 0.0;
    Fz[ix][iy][iz] = 0.0;
  }

}

// device function to set the 3D volume
__global__
void allenCahn(double phinew[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
               double phiold[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
               double uold[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
               double Fx[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
               double Fy[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
               double Fz[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
               double epsilon, double W0, double tau0, double lambda,
               double dt, double dx, double dy, double dz)
{
  unsigned iz = blockIdx.x*blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
  unsigned iy = blockIdx.y*blockDim.y + threadIdx.y;
  unsigned ix = blockIdx.z*blockDim.z + threadIdx.z;

  if ((ix < (DATAXSIZE-1)) && (iy < (DATAYSIZE-1)) &&
      (iz < (DATAZSIZE-1)) && (ix > (0)) &&
      (iy > (0)) && (iz > (0))) {

    double phix = GradientX(phiold,dx,dy,dz,ix,iy,iz);
    double phiy = GradientY(phiold,dx,dy,dz,ix,iy,iz);
    double phiz = GradientZ(phiold,dx,dy,dz,ix,iy,iz);

    phinew[ix][iy][iz] = phiold[ix][iy][iz] +
     (dt / taun(phix,phiy,phiz,epsilon,tau0)) *
     (Divergence(Fx,Fy,Fz,dx,dy,dz,ix,iy,iz) -
      dFphi(phiold[ix][iy][iz], uold[ix][iy][iz],lambda));
  }
}

__global__
void boundaryConditionsPhi(double phinew[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE])
{
  unsigned iz = blockIdx.x*blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
  unsigned iy = blockIdx.y*blockDim.y + threadIdx.y;
  unsigned ix = blockIdx.z*blockDim.z + threadIdx.z;
  if (iz >= DATAZSIZE || iy >= DATAYSIZE || ix >= DATAXSIZE) return;

  if (ix == 0){
    phinew[ix][iy][iz] = -1.0;
  }
  else if (ix == DATAXSIZE-1){
    phinew[ix][iy][iz] = -1.0;
  }
  else if (iy == 0){
    phinew[ix][iy][iz] = -1.0;
  }
  else if (iy == DATAYSIZE-1){
    phinew[ix][iy][iz] = -1.0;
  }
  else if (iz == 0){
    phinew[ix][iy][iz] = -1.0;
  }
  else if (iz == DATAZSIZE-1){
    phinew[ix][iy][iz] = -1.0;
  }
}

__global__
void thermalEquation(double unew[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
                     double uold[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
                     double phinew[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
                     double phiold[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
                     double D, double dt, double dx, double dy, double dz)
{
  unsigned iz = blockIdx.x*blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
  unsigned iy = blockIdx.y*blockDim.y + threadIdx.y;
  unsigned ix = blockIdx.z*blockDim.z + threadIdx.z;

  if ((ix < (DATAXSIZE-1)) && (iy < (DATAYSIZE-1)) &&
      (iz < (DATAZSIZE-1)) && (ix > (0)) &&
      (iy > (0)) && (iz > (0))){
    unew[ix][iy][iz] = uold[ix][iy][iz] +
      0.5*(phinew[ix][iy][iz]- phiold[ix][iy][iz]) +
      dt * D * Laplacian(uold,dx,dy,dz,ix,iy,iz);
  }
}

__global__
void boundaryConditionsU(double unew[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE], double delta)
{
  unsigned iz = blockIdx.x*blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
  unsigned iy = blockIdx.y*blockDim.y + threadIdx.y;
  unsigned ix = blockIdx.z*blockDim.z + threadIdx.z;
  if (iz >= DATAZSIZE || iy >= DATAYSIZE || ix >= DATAXSIZE) return;

  if (ix == 0){
    unew[ix][iy][iz] =  -delta;
  }
  else if (ix == DATAXSIZE-1){
    unew[ix][iy][iz] =  -delta;
  }
  else if (iy == 0){
    unew[ix][iy][iz] =  -delta;
  }
  else if (iy == DATAYSIZE-1){
    unew[ix][iy][iz] =  -delta;
  }
  else if (iz == 0){
    unew[ix][iy][iz] =  -delta;
  }
  else if (iz == DATAZSIZE-1){
    unew[ix][iy][iz] =  -delta;
  }
}

__global__
void swapGrid(double cnew[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
              double cold[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE])
{
  unsigned iz = blockIdx.x*blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
  unsigned iy = blockIdx.y*blockDim.y + threadIdx.y;
  unsigned ix = blockIdx.z*blockDim.z + threadIdx.z;
  if (iz >= DATAZSIZE || iy >= DATAYSIZE || ix >= DATAXSIZE) return;

  double tmp = cnew[ix][iy][iz];
  cnew[ix][iy][iz] = cold[ix][iy][iz];
  cold[ix][iy][iz] = tmp;
}

void initializationPhi(double phi[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE], double r0)
{
#ifdef _OPENMP
  #pragma omp parallel for collapse(3)
#endif
  for (int idx = 0; idx < DATAXSIZE; idx++) {
    for (int idy = 0; idy < DATAYSIZE; idy++) {
      for (int idz = 0; idz < DATAZSIZE; idz++) {
        double r = std::sqrt(SQ(idx-0.5*DATAXSIZE) + SQ(idy-0.5*DATAYSIZE) + SQ(idz-0.5*DATAZSIZE));
        if (r < r0){
          phi[idx][idy][idz] = 1.0;
        }
        else
        {
          phi[idx][idy][idz] = -1.0;
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

void initializationU(double u[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE], double r0, double delta)
{
#ifdef _OPENMP
  #pragma omp parallel for collapse(3)
#endif
  for (int idx = 0; idx < DATAXSIZE; idx++) {
    for (int idy = 0; idy < DATAYSIZE; idy++) {
      for (int idz = 0; idz < DATAZSIZE; idz++) {
        double r = std::sqrt(SQ(idx-0.5*DATAXSIZE) + SQ(idy-0.5*DATAYSIZE) + SQ(idz-0.5*DATAZSIZE));
        if (r < r0) {
          u[idx][idy][idz] = 0.0;
        }
        else
        {
          u[idx][idy][idz] = -delta * (1.0 - std::exp(-(r-r0)));
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

int main(int argc, char *argv[])
{
  const int num_steps = atoi(argv[1]);  //6000;
  const double dx = 0.4;
  const double dy = 0.4;
  const double dz = 0.4;
  const double dt = 0.01;
  const double delta = 0.8;
  const double r0 = 5.0;
  const double epsilon = 0.07;
  const double W0 = 1.0;
  const double beta0 = 0.0;
  const double D = 2.0;
  const double d0 = 0.5;
  const double a1 = 1.25 / std::sqrt(2.0);
  const double a2 = 0.64;
  const double lambda = (W0*a1)/(d0);
  const double tau0 = ((W0*W0*W0*a1*a2)/(d0*D)) + ((W0*W0*beta0)/(d0));

  // overall data set sizes
  const int nx = DATAXSIZE;
  const int ny = DATAYSIZE;
  const int nz = DATAZSIZE;
  const int vol = nx * ny * nz;
  const size_t vol_in_bytes = sizeof(double) * vol;

  // pointers for data set storage via malloc
  nRarray *phi_host;
  nRarray *d_phiold;
  nRarray *u_host;
  nRarray *d_phinew;
  nRarray *d_uold;
  nRarray *d_unew;
  nRarray *d_Fx;
  nRarray *d_Fy;
  nRarray *d_Fz;

  phi_host = (nRarray *)malloc(vol_in_bytes);
  u_host = (nRarray *)malloc(vol_in_bytes);

  initializationPhi(phi_host,r0);
  initializationU(u_host,r0,delta);

#ifdef VERIFY
  nRarray *phi_ref = (nRarray *)malloc(vol_in_bytes);
  nRarray *u_ref = (nRarray *)malloc(vol_in_bytes);
  memcpy(phi_ref, phi_host, vol_in_bytes);
  memcpy(u_ref, u_host, vol_in_bytes);
  reference(phi_ref, u_ref, vol, num_steps);
#endif

  auto offload_start = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();

  // define the chunk sizes that each threadblock will work on
  dim3 grid ((DATAZSIZE+7)/8, (DATAYSIZE+7)/8, (DATAXSIZE+3)/4);
  dim3 block (8, 8, 4);

  // allocate GPU device buffers
  cudaMalloc((void **) &d_phiold, vol_in_bytes);
  cudaMalloc((void **) &d_phinew, vol_in_bytes);
  cudaMalloc((void **) &d_uold, vol_in_bytes);
  cudaMalloc((void **) &d_unew, vol_in_bytes);
  cudaMalloc((void **) &d_Fx, vol_in_bytes);
  cudaMalloc((void **) &d_Fy, vol_in_bytes);
  cudaMalloc((void **) &d_Fz, vol_in_bytes);

  cudaMemcpy(d_phiold, phi_host, vol_in_bytes, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice);
  cudaMemcpy(d_uold, u_host, vol_in_bytes, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice);

  int t = 0;

  cudaDeviceSynchronize();
  auto start = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();

  while (t <= num_steps) {

    calculateForce<<<grid, block>>>(d_phiold,d_Fx,d_Fy,d_Fz,
                                    dx,dy,dz,epsilon,W0,tau0);

    allenCahn<<<grid, block>>>(d_phinew,d_phiold,d_uold,
                               d_Fx,d_Fy,d_Fz,
                               epsilon,W0,tau0,lambda,
                               dt,dx,dy,dz);

    boundaryConditionsPhi<<<grid, block>>>(d_phinew);

    thermalEquation<<<grid, block>>>(d_unew,d_uold,d_phinew,d_phiold,
                                     D,dt,dx,dy,dz);

    boundaryConditionsU<<<grid, block>>>(d_unew,delta);

    swapGrid<<<grid, block>>>(d_phinew, d_phiold);

    swapGrid<<<grid, block>>>(d_unew, d_uold);

    t++;
  }

  cudaDeviceSynchronize();
  auto end = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
  auto time = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::nanoseconds>(end - start).count();
  printf("Total kernel execution time: %.3f (ms)\n", time * 1e-6f);

  cudaMemcpy(phi_host, d_phiold, vol_in_bytes, cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost);
  cudaMemcpy(u_host, d_uold, vol_in_bytes, cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost);

  cudaFree(d_phiold);
  cudaFree(d_phinew);
  cudaFree(d_uold);
  cudaFree(d_unew);
  cudaFree(d_Fx);
  cudaFree(d_Fy);
  cudaFree(d_Fz);

  auto offload_end = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
  auto offload_time = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::nanoseconds>(offload_end - offload_start).count();
  printf("Offload time: %.3f (ms)\n", offload_time * 1e-6f);

#ifdef VERIFY
  bool ok = true;
  for (int idx = 0; idx < nx; idx++)
    for (int idy = 0; idy < ny; idy++)
      for (int idz = 0; idz < nz; idz++) {
        if (fabs(phi_ref[idx][idy][idz] - phi_host[idx][idy][idz]) > 1e-3) {
          ok = false; printf("phi: %lf %lf\n", phi_ref[idx][idy][idz], phi_host[idx][idy][idz]);
	}
        if (fabs(u_ref[idx][idy][idz] - u_host[idx][idy][idz]) > 1e-3) {
          ok = false; printf("u: %lf %lf\n", u_ref[idx][idy][idz], u_host[idx][idy][idz]);
        }
      }
  printf("%s\n", ok ? "PASS" : "FAIL");
  free(phi_ref);
  free(u_ref);
#endif

  free(phi_host);
  free(u_host);
  return 0;
}

#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <math.h>
#include <chrono>
#include <cuda.h>

//define the data set size (cubic volume)
#define DATAXSIZE 400
#define DATAYSIZE 400
#define DATAZSIZE 400

typedef double nRarray[DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE];

// square
#define SQ(x) ((x)*(x))

#ifdef VERIFY
#include <string.h>
#include "reference.h"
#endif

__device__
double dFphi(double phi, double u, double lambda)
{
  return (-phi*(1.0-phi*phi)+lambda*u*(1.0-phi*phi)*(1.0-phi*phi));
}

__device__
double GradientX(double phi[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
                 double dx, double dy, double dz, int x, int y, int z)
{
  return (phi[x+1][y][z] - phi[x-1][y][z]) / (2.0*dx);
}

__device__
double GradientY(double phi[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
                 double dx, double dy, double dz, int x, int y, int z)
{
  return (phi[x][y+1][z] - phi[x][y-1][z]) / (2.0*dy);
}

__device__
double GradientZ(double phi[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
                 double dx, double dy, double dz, int x, int y, int z)
{
  return (phi[x][y][z+1] - phi[x][y][z-1]) / (2.0*dz);
}

__device__
double Divergence(double phix[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
                  double phiy[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
                  double phiz[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
                  double dx, double dy, double dz, int x, int y, int z)
{
  return GradientX(phix,dx,dy,dz,x,y,z) +
         GradientY(phiy,dx,dy,dz,x,y,z) +
         GradientZ(phiz,dx,dy,dz,x,y,z);
}

__device__
double Laplacian(double phi[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
                 double dx, double dy, double dz, int x, int y, int z)
{
  double phixx = (phi[x+1][y][z] + phi[x-1][y][z] - 2.0 * phi[x][y][z]) / SQ(dx);
  double phiyy = (phi[x][y+1][z] + phi[x][y-1][z] - 2.0 * phi[x][y][z]) / SQ(dy);
  double phizz = (phi[x][y][z+1] + phi[x][y][z-1] - 2.0 * phi[x][y][z]) / SQ(dz);
  return phixx + phiyy + phizz;
}

__device__
double An(double phix, double phiy, double phiz, double epsilon)
{
  if (phix != 0.0 || phiy != 0.0 || phiz != 0.0){
    return ((1.0 - 3.0 * epsilon) * (1.0 + (((4.0 * epsilon) / (1.0-3.0*epsilon))*
           ((SQ(phix)*SQ(phix)+SQ(phiy)*SQ(phiy)+SQ(phiz)*SQ(phiz)) /
           ((SQ(phix)+SQ(phiy)+SQ(phiz))*(SQ(phix)+SQ(phiy)+SQ(phiz)))))));
  }
  else
  {
    return (1.0-((5.0/3.0)*epsilon));
  }
}

__device__
double Wn(double phix, double phiy, double phiz, double epsilon, double W0)
{
  return (W0*An(phix,phiy,phiz,epsilon));
}

__device__
double taun(double phix, double phiy, double phiz, double epsilon, double tau0)
{
  return tau0 * SQ(An(phix,phiy,phiz,epsilon));
}

__device__
double dFunc(double l, double m, double n)
{
  if (l != 0.0 || m != 0.0 || n != 0.0){
    return (((l*l*l*(SQ(m)+SQ(n)))-(l*(SQ(m)*SQ(m)+SQ(n)*SQ(n)))) /
            ((SQ(l)+SQ(m)+SQ(n))*(SQ(l)+SQ(m)+SQ(n))));
  }
  else
  {
    return 0.0;
  }
}

__global__
void calculateForce(double phi[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
                    double Fx[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
                    double Fy[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
                    double Fz[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
                    double dx, double dy, double dz,
                    double epsilon, double W0, double tau0)
{

  unsigned iz = blockIdx.x*blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
  unsigned iy = blockIdx.y*blockDim.y + threadIdx.y;
  unsigned ix = blockIdx.z*blockDim.z + threadIdx.z;

  if ((ix < (DATAXSIZE-1)) && (iy < (DATAYSIZE-1)) &&
      (iz < (DATAZSIZE-1)) && (ix > (0)) &&
      (iy > (0)) && (iz > (0))) {

    double phix = GradientX(phi,dx,dy,dz,ix,iy,iz);
    double phiy = GradientY(phi,dx,dy,dz,ix,iy,iz);
    double phiz = GradientZ(phi,dx,dy,dz,ix,iy,iz);
    double sqGphi = SQ(phix) + SQ(phiy) + SQ(phiz);
    double c = 16.0 * W0 * epsilon;
    double w = Wn(phix,phiy,phiz,epsilon,W0);
    double w2 = SQ(w);


    Fx[ix][iy][iz] = w2 * phix + sqGphi * w * c * dFunc(phix,phiy,phiz);
    Fy[ix][iy][iz] = w2 * phiy + sqGphi * w * c * dFunc(phiy,phiz,phix);
    Fz[ix][iy][iz] = w2 * phiz + sqGphi * w * c * dFunc(phiz,phix,phiy);
  }
  else
  {
    Fx[ix][iy][iz] = 0.0;
    Fy[ix][iy][iz] = 0.0;
    Fz[ix][iy][iz] = 0.0;
  }

}

// device function to set the 3D volume
__global__
void allenCahn(double phinew[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
               double phiold[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
               double uold[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
               double Fx[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
               double Fy[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
               double Fz[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
               double epsilon, double W0, double tau0, double lambda,
               double dt, double dx, double dy, double dz)
{
  unsigned iz = blockIdx.x*blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
  unsigned iy = blockIdx.y*blockDim.y + threadIdx.y;
  unsigned ix = blockIdx.z*blockDim.z + threadIdx.z;

  if ((ix < (DATAXSIZE-1)) && (iy < (DATAYSIZE-1)) &&
      (iz < (DATAZSIZE-1)) && (ix > (0)) &&
      (iy > (0)) && (iz > (0))) {

    double phix = GradientX(phiold,dx,dy,dz,ix,iy,iz);
    double phiy = GradientY(phiold,dx,dy,dz,ix,iy,iz);
    double phiz = GradientZ(phiold,dx,dy,dz,ix,iy,iz);

    phinew[ix][iy][iz] = phiold[ix][iy][iz] +
     (dt / taun(phix,phiy,phiz,epsilon,tau0)) *
     (Divergence(Fx,Fy,Fz,dx,dy,dz,ix,iy,iz) -
      dFphi(phiold[ix][iy][iz], uold[ix][iy][iz],lambda));
  }
}

__global__
void boundaryConditionsPhi(double phinew[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE])
{
  unsigned iz = blockIdx.x*blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
  unsigned iy = blockIdx.y*blockDim.y + threadIdx.y;
  unsigned ix = blockIdx.z*blockDim.z + threadIdx.z;
  if (iz >= DATAZSIZE || iy >= DATAYSIZE || ix >= DATAXSIZE) return;

  if (ix == 0){
    phinew[ix][iy][iz] = -1.0;
  }
  else if (ix == DATAXSIZE-1){
    phinew[ix][iy][iz] = -1.0;
  }
  else if (iy == 0){
    phinew[ix][iy][iz] = -1.0;
  }
  else if (iy == DATAYSIZE-1){
    phinew[ix][iy][iz] = -1.0;
  }
  else if (iz == 0){
    phinew[ix][iy][iz] = -1.0;
  }
  else if (iz == DATAZSIZE-1){
    phinew[ix][iy][iz] = -1.0;
  }
}

__global__
void thermalEquation(double unew[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
                     double uold[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
                     double phinew[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
                     double phiold[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
                     double D, double dt, double dx, double dy, double dz)
{
  unsigned iz = blockIdx.x*blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
  unsigned iy = blockIdx.y*blockDim.y + threadIdx.y;
  unsigned ix = blockIdx.z*blockDim.z + threadIdx.z;

  if ((ix < (DATAXSIZE-1)) && (iy < (DATAYSIZE-1)) &&
      (iz < (DATAZSIZE-1)) && (ix > (0)) &&
      (iy > (0)) && (iz > (0))){
    unew[ix][iy][iz] = uold[ix][iy][iz] +
      0.5*(phinew[ix][iy][iz]- phiold[ix][iy][iz]) +
      dt * D * Laplacian(uold,dx,dy,dz,ix,iy,iz);
  }
}

__global__
void boundaryConditionsU(double unew[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE], double delta)
{
  unsigned iz = blockIdx.x*blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
  unsigned iy = blockIdx.y*blockDim.y + threadIdx.y;
  unsigned ix = blockIdx.z*blockDim.z + threadIdx.z;
  if (iz >= DATAZSIZE || iy >= DATAYSIZE || ix >= DATAXSIZE) return;

  if (ix == 0){
    unew[ix][iy][iz] =  -delta;
  }
  else if (ix == DATAXSIZE-1){
    unew[ix][iy][iz] =  -delta;
  }
  else if (iy == 0){
    unew[ix][iy][iz] =  -delta;
  }
  else if (iy == DATAYSIZE-1){
    unew[ix][iy][iz] =  -delta;
  }
  else if (iz == 0){
    unew[ix][iy][iz] =  -delta;
  }
  else if (iz == DATAZSIZE-1){
    unew[ix][iy][iz] =  -delta;
  }
}

__global__
void swapGrid(double cnew[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
              double cold[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE])
{
  unsigned iz = blockIdx.x*blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
  unsigned iy = blockIdx.y*blockDim.y + threadIdx.y;
  unsigned ix = blockIdx.z*blockDim.z + threadIdx.z;
  if (iz >= DATAZSIZE || iy >= DATAYSIZE || ix >= DATAXSIZE) return;

  double tmp = cnew[ix][iy][iz];
  cnew[ix][iy][iz] = cold[ix][iy][iz];
  cold[ix][iy][iz] = tmp;
}

void initializationPhi(double phi[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE], double r0)
{
#ifdef _OPENMP
  #pragma omp parallel for collapse(3)
#endif
  for (int idx = 0; idx < DATAXSIZE; idx++) {
    for (int idy = 0; idy < DATAYSIZE; idy++) {
      for (int idz = 0; idz < DATAZSIZE; idz++) {
        double r = std::sqrt(SQ(idx-0.5*DATAXSIZE) + SQ(idy-0.5*DATAYSIZE) + SQ(idz-0.5*DATAZSIZE));
        if (r < r0){
          phi[idx][idy][idz] = 1.0;
        }
        else
        {
          phi[idx][idy][idz] = -1.0;
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

void initializationU(double u[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE], double r0, double delta)
{
#ifdef _OPENMP
  #pragma omp parallel for collapse(3)
#endif
  for (int idx = 0; idx < DATAXSIZE; idx++) {
    for (int idy = 0; idy < DATAYSIZE; idy++) {
      for (int idz = 0; idz < DATAZSIZE; idz++) {
        double r = std::sqrt(SQ(idx-0.5*DATAXSIZE) + SQ(idy-0.5*DATAYSIZE) + SQ(idz-0.5*DATAZSIZE));
        if (r < r0) {
          u[idx][idy][idz] = 0.0;
        }
        else
        {
          u[idx][idy][idz] = -delta * (1.0 - std::exp(-(r-r0)));
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

int main(int argc, char *argv[])
{
  const int num_steps = atoi(argv[1]);  //6000;
  const double dx = 0.4;
  const double dy = 0.4;
  const double dz = 0.4;
  const double dt = 0.01;
  const double delta = 0.8;
  const double r0 = 5.0;
  const double epsilon = 0.07;
  const double W0 = 1.0;
  const double beta0 = 0.0;
  const double D = 2.0;
  const double d0 = 0.5;
  const double a1 = 1.25 / std::sqrt(2.0);
  const double a2 = 0.64;
  const double lambda = (W0*a1)/(d0);
  const double tau0 = ((W0*W0*W0*a1*a2)/(d0*D)) + ((W0*W0*beta0)/(d0));

  // overall data set sizes
  const int nx = DATAXSIZE;
  const int ny = DATAYSIZE;
  const int nz = DATAZSIZE;
  const int vol = nx * ny * nz;
  const size_t vol_in_bytes = sizeof(double) * vol;

  // pointers for data set storage via malloc
  nRarray *phi_host;
  nRarray *d_phiold;
  nRarray *u_host;
  nRarray *d_phinew;
  nRarray *d_uold;
  nRarray *d_unew;
  nRarray *d_Fx;
  nRarray *d_Fy;
  nRarray *d_Fz;

  phi_host = (nRarray *)malloc(vol_in_bytes);
  u_host = (nRarray *)malloc(vol_in_bytes);

  initializationPhi(phi_host,r0);
  initializationU(u_host,r0,delta);

#ifdef VERIFY
  nRarray *phi_ref = (nRarray *)malloc(vol_in_bytes);
  nRarray *u_ref = (nRarray *)malloc(vol_in_bytes);
  memcpy(phi_ref, phi_host, vol_in_bytes);
  memcpy(u_ref, u_host, vol_in_bytes);
  reference(phi_ref, u_ref, vol, num_steps);
#endif

  auto offload_start = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();

  // define the chunk sizes that each threadblock will work on
  dim3 grid ((DATAZSIZE+7)/8, (DATAYSIZE+7)/8, (DATAXSIZE+3)/4);
  dim3 block (8, 8, 4);

  // allocate GPU device buffers
  cudaMalloc((void **) &d_phiold, vol_in_bytes);
  cudaMalloc((void **) &d_phinew, vol_in_bytes);
  cudaMalloc((void **) &d_uold, vol_in_bytes);
  cudaMalloc((void **) &d_unew, vol_in_bytes);
  cudaMalloc((void **) &d_Fx, vol_in_bytes);
  cudaMalloc((void **) &d_Fy, vol_in_bytes);
  cudaMalloc((void **) &d_Fz, vol_in_bytes);

  cudaMemcpy(d_phiold, phi_host, vol_in_bytes, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice);
  cudaMemcpy(d_uold, u_host, vol_in_bytes, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice);

  int t = 0;

  cudaDeviceSynchronize();
  auto start = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();

  while (t <= num_steps) {

    calculateForce<<<grid, block>>>(d_phiold,d_Fx,d_Fy,d_Fz,
                                    dx,dy,dz,epsilon,W0,tau0);

    allenCahn<<<grid, block>>>(d_phinew,d_phiold,d_uold,
                               d_Fx,d_Fy,d_Fz,
                               epsilon,W0,tau0,lambda,
                               dt,dx,dy,dz);

    boundaryConditionsPhi<<<grid, block>>>(d_phinew);

    thermalEquation<<<grid, block>>>(d_unew,d_uold,d_phinew,d_phiold,
                                     D,dt,dx,dy,dz);

    boundaryConditionsU<<<grid, block>>>(d_unew,delta);

    swapGrid<<<grid, block>>>(d_phinew, d_phiold);

    swapGrid<<<grid, block>>>(d_unew, d_uold);

    t++;
  }

  cudaDeviceSynchronize();
  auto end = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
  auto time = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::nanoseconds>(end - start).count();
  printf("Total kernel execution time: %.3f (ms)\n", time * 1e-6f);

  cudaMemcpy(phi_host, d_phiold, vol_in_bytes, cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost);
  cudaMemcpy(u_host, d_uold, vol_in_bytes, cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost);

  cudaFree(d_phiold);
  cudaFree(d_phinew);
  cudaFree(d_uold);
  cudaFree(d_unew);
  cudaFree(d_Fx);
  cudaFree(d_Fy);
  cudaFree(d_Fz);

  auto offload_end = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
  auto offload_time = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::nanoseconds>(offload_end - offload_start).count();
  printf("Offload time: %.3f (ms)\n", offload_time * 1e-6f);

#ifdef VERIFY
  bool ok = true;
  for (int idx = 0; idx < nx; idx++)
    for (int idy = 0; idy < ny; idy++)
      for (int idz = 0; idz < nz; idz++) {
        if (fabs(phi_ref[idx][idy][idz] - phi_host[idx][idy][idz]) > 1e-3) {
          ok = false; printf("phi: %lf %lf\n", phi_ref[idx][idy][idz], phi_host[idx][idy][idz]);
	}
        if (fabs(u_ref[idx][idy][idz] - u_host[idx][idy][idz]) > 1e-3) {
          ok = false; printf("u: %lf %lf\n", u_ref[idx][idy][idz], u_host[idx][idy][idz]);
        }
      }
  printf("%s\n", ok ? "PASS" : "FAIL");
  free(phi_ref);
  free(u_ref);
#endif

  free(phi_host);
  free(u_host);
  return 0;
}

### Counting Compiler-Generated FP16 and FP32 Instructions
- Count compiler-generated arithmetic instructions if they execute, even when they originate from helper routines, lowered math-library calls, constant materialization, or implementation details rather than explicit source-level arithmetic.
- The compiler may insert packed FP16 instructions such as HFMA2 / HFMA2_32I for constant or zero materialization on some GPU architectures instead of using MOV-family instructions. If these execute, count them as real FP16 arithmetic in the final estimate: each HFMA2 contributes 4 FP16 FLOPs, but this behavior is architecture- and ptxas-dependent, so infer it conservatively when SASS is unavailable.
- Packed FP16 fused multiply-add instructions contribute multiple FP16 FLOPs per instruction. Lower-precision helper instructions used to implement higher-precision or transcendental operations still count toward the precision at which they execute.
- When SASS is available, count the arithmetic instructions on the taken execution path and scale by how many times that path executes. When SASS is not available, acknowledge that source-only counting may under-estimate lowered helper work and provide the best defensible estimate from the source.
- Compilers may also eliminate common subexpressions or reuse previously computed values, which can reduce the true FLOP count. Use the source and SASS together to avoid over-counting optimized-away work.

### Counting FLOPs from Transcendental and Math Library Functions

Count every FFMA, FMUL, FADD, FSETP, MUFU.RCP, MUFU.RSQ, MUFU.RCP64H, etc. that executes on the taken path.

## Section 3: DRAM Read and Write Byte Counting

### General Principles
- Estimate DRAM bytes read and DRAM bytes written for the same first invocation of the kernel.
- Count only memory traffic attributable to that invocation, not later kernel launches, host-device transfers, or deferred effects outside the invocation being analyzed.
- Although the source may show many reads and writes, the compiler may optimize, combine, or eliminate some of them, so reason carefully from the executed source path when estimating actual global-memory traffic.

### Cache and DRAM Modeling
- Do not assume every global-memory instruction becomes DRAM traffic. Some LDG operations may be serviced by the L2 cache instead of DRAM, so only count the loads that correspond to DRAM accesses when estimating dram_bytes_read_count.
- For writes, only count the bytes that go beyond the L2 cache and actually reach DRAM when estimating dram_bytes_written_count. Consider the L2 cache size from <gpu_roofline_specs> together with the amount of store traffic to estimate whether written data fits in cache or spills through to DRAM.
- In many cases, if all the writes fit in the L2 cache, then dram_bytes_written_count will be zero, even if the source code shows many store instructions. Recall that the CUDA L2 cache is a write-back cache at the device-scope visibility, so it does not flush to the DRAM until evictions occur. Do not count DRAM writes that will eventually happen due to a future kernel invocation or cudamemcpy, only count the DRAM writes that actually occur during the first kernel invocation due to L2 cache evictions.

### Distinguishing Unique Footprint from Total Traffic
- Distinguish the unique data footprint from total load/store traffic. A kernel may execute many memory instructions while repeatedly touching the same cache lines.
- For DRAM read estimation: if the unique read footprint (distinct cache lines touched) fits in L2, then after the first compulsory miss, subsequent reads of the same addresses in inner-loop iterations will hit in cache. In this case, DRAM bytes read ≈ unique footprint, not total_loads × element_size.
- For DRAM write estimation: if the unique write footprint fits in L2, then repeated stores to the same addresses will overwrite the same cache lines without eviction, and DRAM bytes written ≈ 0 during the kernel (the dirty lines remain in L2 until a later eviction event).
- Always compute both the unique footprint and the total traffic, then use the L2 cache size to determine which estimate is appropriate.

### Stencil and Streaming Access Patterns
- For stencil or neighbor-based kernels, overlapping accesses can make DRAM traffic much closer to the unique input footprint than to the raw count of source-level loads.
- When the working set is much larger than L2, account for the possibility of cache-line eviction and refetch rather than assuming perfect reuse.
- When the working set fits in L2, DRAM traffic may be close to the unique footprint loaded once and then reused from cache.

### Write Traffic Amplification
- For streaming write patterns where the output footprint is larger than L2, actual DRAM write traffic can exceed the unique write footprint because of cache behavior and write-allocation effects. Use the unique footprint as a baseline and adjust only when the access pattern or hardware evidence justifies it.

#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <math.h>
#include <chrono>
#include <cuda.h>

//define the data set size (cubic volume)
#define DATAXSIZE 400
#define DATAYSIZE 400
#define DATAZSIZE 400

typedef double nRarray[DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE];

// square
#define SQ(x) ((x)*(x))

#ifdef VERIFY
#include <string.h>
#include "reference.h"
#endif

__device__
double dFphi(double phi, double u, double lambda)
{
  return (-phi*(1.0-phi*phi)+lambda*u*(1.0-phi*phi)*(1.0-phi*phi));
}

__device__
double GradientX(double phi[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
                 double dx, double dy, double dz, int x, int y, int z)
{
  return (phi[x+1][y][z] - phi[x-1][y][z]) / (2.0*dx);
}

__device__
double GradientY(double phi[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
                 double dx, double dy, double dz, int x, int y, int z)
{
  return (phi[x][y+1][z] - phi[x][y-1][z]) / (2.0*dy);
}

__device__
double GradientZ(double phi[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
                 double dx, double dy, double dz, int x, int y, int z)
{
  return (phi[x][y][z+1] - phi[x][y][z-1]) / (2.0*dz);
}

__device__
double Divergence(double phix[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
                  double phiy[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
                  double phiz[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
                  double dx, double dy, double dz, int x, int y, int z)
{
  return GradientX(phix,dx,dy,dz,x,y,z) +
         GradientY(phiy,dx,dy,dz,x,y,z) +
         GradientZ(phiz,dx,dy,dz,x,y,z);
}

__device__
double Laplacian(double phi[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
                 double dx, double dy, double dz, int x, int y, int z)
{
  double phixx = (phi[x+1][y][z] + phi[x-1][y][z] - 2.0 * phi[x][y][z]) / SQ(dx);
  double phiyy = (phi[x][y+1][z] + phi[x][y-1][z] - 2.0 * phi[x][y][z]) / SQ(dy);
  double phizz = (phi[x][y][z+1] + phi[x][y][z-1] - 2.0 * phi[x][y][z]) / SQ(dz);
  return phixx + phiyy + phizz;
}

__device__
double An(double phix, double phiy, double phiz, double epsilon)
{
  if (phix != 0.0 || phiy != 0.0 || phiz != 0.0){
    return ((1.0 - 3.0 * epsilon) * (1.0 + (((4.0 * epsilon) / (1.0-3.0*epsilon))*
           ((SQ(phix)*SQ(phix)+SQ(phiy)*SQ(phiy)+SQ(phiz)*SQ(phiz)) /
           ((SQ(phix)+SQ(phiy)+SQ(phiz))*(SQ(phix)+SQ(phiy)+SQ(phiz)))))));
  }
  else
  {
    return (1.0-((5.0/3.0)*epsilon));
  }
}

__device__
double Wn(double phix, double phiy, double phiz, double epsilon, double W0)
{
  return (W0*An(phix,phiy,phiz,epsilon));
}

__device__
double taun(double phix, double phiy, double phiz, double epsilon, double tau0)
{
  return tau0 * SQ(An(phix,phiy,phiz,epsilon));
}

__device__
double dFunc(double l, double m, double n)
{
  if (l != 0.0 || m != 0.0 || n != 0.0){
    return (((l*l*l*(SQ(m)+SQ(n)))-(l*(SQ(m)*SQ(m)+SQ(n)*SQ(n)))) /
            ((SQ(l)+SQ(m)+SQ(n))*(SQ(l)+SQ(m)+SQ(n))));
  }
  else
  {
    return 0.0;
  }
}

__global__
void calculateForce(double phi[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
                    double Fx[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
                    double Fy[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
                    double Fz[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
                    double dx, double dy, double dz,
                    double epsilon, double W0, double tau0)
{

  unsigned iz = blockIdx.x*blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
  unsigned iy = blockIdx.y*blockDim.y + threadIdx.y;
  unsigned ix = blockIdx.z*blockDim.z + threadIdx.z;

  if ((ix < (DATAXSIZE-1)) && (iy < (DATAYSIZE-1)) &&
      (iz < (DATAZSIZE-1)) && (ix > (0)) &&
      (iy > (0)) && (iz > (0))) {

    double phix = GradientX(phi,dx,dy,dz,ix,iy,iz);
    double phiy = GradientY(phi,dx,dy,dz,ix,iy,iz);
    double phiz = GradientZ(phi,dx,dy,dz,ix,iy,iz);
    double sqGphi = SQ(phix) + SQ(phiy) + SQ(phiz);
    double c = 16.0 * W0 * epsilon;
    double w = Wn(phix,phiy,phiz,epsilon,W0);
    double w2 = SQ(w);


    Fx[ix][iy][iz] = w2 * phix + sqGphi * w * c * dFunc(phix,phiy,phiz);
    Fy[ix][iy][iz] = w2 * phiy + sqGphi * w * c * dFunc(phiy,phiz,phix);
    Fz[ix][iy][iz] = w2 * phiz + sqGphi * w * c * dFunc(phiz,phix,phiy);
  }
  else
  {
    Fx[ix][iy][iz] = 0.0;
    Fy[ix][iy][iz] = 0.0;
    Fz[ix][iy][iz] = 0.0;
  }

}

// device function to set the 3D volume
__global__
void allenCahn(double phinew[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
               double phiold[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
               double uold[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
               double Fx[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
               double Fy[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
               double Fz[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
               double epsilon, double W0, double tau0, double lambda,
               double dt, double dx, double dy, double dz)
{
  unsigned iz = blockIdx.x*blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
  unsigned iy = blockIdx.y*blockDim.y + threadIdx.y;
  unsigned ix = blockIdx.z*blockDim.z + threadIdx.z;

  if ((ix < (DATAXSIZE-1)) && (iy < (DATAYSIZE-1)) &&
      (iz < (DATAZSIZE-1)) && (ix > (0)) &&
      (iy > (0)) && (iz > (0))) {

    double phix = GradientX(phiold,dx,dy,dz,ix,iy,iz);
    double phiy = GradientY(phiold,dx,dy,dz,ix,iy,iz);
    double phiz = GradientZ(phiold,dx,dy,dz,ix,iy,iz);

    phinew[ix][iy][iz] = phiold[ix][iy][iz] +
     (dt / taun(phix,phiy,phiz,epsilon,tau0)) *
     (Divergence(Fx,Fy,Fz,dx,dy,dz,ix,iy,iz) -
      dFphi(phiold[ix][iy][iz], uold[ix][iy][iz],lambda));
  }
}

__global__
void boundaryConditionsPhi(double phinew[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE])
{
  unsigned iz = blockIdx.x*blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
  unsigned iy = blockIdx.y*blockDim.y + threadIdx.y;
  unsigned ix = blockIdx.z*blockDim.z + threadIdx.z;
  if (iz >= DATAZSIZE || iy >= DATAYSIZE || ix >= DATAXSIZE) return;

  if (ix == 0){
    phinew[ix][iy][iz] = -1.0;
  }
  else if (ix == DATAXSIZE-1){
    phinew[ix][iy][iz] = -1.0;
  }
  else if (iy == 0){
    phinew[ix][iy][iz] = -1.0;
  }
  else if (iy == DATAYSIZE-1){
    phinew[ix][iy][iz] = -1.0;
  }
  else if (iz == 0){
    phinew[ix][iy][iz] = -1.0;
  }
  else if (iz == DATAZSIZE-1){
    phinew[ix][iy][iz] = -1.0;
  }
}

__global__
void thermalEquation(double unew[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
                     double uold[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
                     double phinew[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
                     double phiold[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
                     double D, double dt, double dx, double dy, double dz)
{
  unsigned iz = blockIdx.x*blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
  unsigned iy = blockIdx.y*blockDim.y + threadIdx.y;
  unsigned ix = blockIdx.z*blockDim.z + threadIdx.z;

  if ((ix < (DATAXSIZE-1)) && (iy < (DATAYSIZE-1)) &&
      (iz < (DATAZSIZE-1)) && (ix > (0)) &&
      (iy > (0)) && (iz > (0))){
    unew[ix][iy][iz] = uold[ix][iy][iz] +
      0.5*(phinew[ix][iy][iz]- phiold[ix][iy][iz]) +
      dt * D * Laplacian(uold,dx,dy,dz,ix,iy,iz);
  }
}

__global__
void boundaryConditionsU(double unew[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE], double delta)
{
  unsigned iz = blockIdx.x*blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
  unsigned iy = blockIdx.y*blockDim.y + threadIdx.y;
  unsigned ix = blockIdx.z*blockDim.z + threadIdx.z;
  if (iz >= DATAZSIZE || iy >= DATAYSIZE || ix >= DATAXSIZE) return;

  if (ix == 0){
    unew[ix][iy][iz] =  -delta;
  }
  else if (ix == DATAXSIZE-1){
    unew[ix][iy][iz] =  -delta;
  }
  else if (iy == 0){
    unew[ix][iy][iz] =  -delta;
  }
  else if (iy == DATAYSIZE-1){
    unew[ix][iy][iz] =  -delta;
  }
  else if (iz == 0){
    unew[ix][iy][iz] =  -delta;
  }
  else if (iz == DATAZSIZE-1){
    unew[ix][iy][iz] =  -delta;
  }
}

__global__
void swapGrid(double cnew[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE],
              double cold[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE])
{
  unsigned iz = blockIdx.x*blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
  unsigned iy = blockIdx.y*blockDim.y + threadIdx.y;
  unsigned ix = blockIdx.z*blockDim.z + threadIdx.z;
  if (iz >= DATAZSIZE || iy >= DATAYSIZE || ix >= DATAXSIZE) return;

  double tmp = cnew[ix][iy][iz];
  cnew[ix][iy][iz] = cold[ix][iy][iz];
  cold[ix][iy][iz] = tmp;
}

void initializationPhi(double phi[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE], double r0)
{
#ifdef _OPENMP
  #pragma omp parallel for collapse(3)
#endif
  for (int idx = 0; idx < DATAXSIZE; idx++) {
    for (int idy = 0; idy < DATAYSIZE; idy++) {
      for (int idz = 0; idz < DATAZSIZE; idz++) {
        double r = std::sqrt(SQ(idx-0.5*DATAXSIZE) + SQ(idy-0.5*DATAYSIZE) + SQ(idz-0.5*DATAZSIZE));
        if (r < r0){
          phi[idx][idy][idz] = 1.0;
        }
        else
        {
          phi[idx][idy][idz] = -1.0;
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

void initializationU(double u[][DATAYSIZE][DATAZSIZE], double r0, double delta)
{
#ifdef _OPENMP
  #pragma omp parallel for collapse(3)
#endif
  for (int idx = 0; idx < DATAXSIZE; idx++) {
    for (int idy = 0; idy < DATAYSIZE; idy++) {
      for (int idz = 0; idz < DATAZSIZE; idz++) {
        double r = std::sqrt(SQ(idx-0.5*DATAXSIZE) + SQ(idy-0.5*DATAYSIZE) + SQ(idz-0.5*DATAZSIZE));
        if (r < r0) {
          u[idx][idy][idz] = 0.0;
        }
        else
        {
          u[idx][idy][idz] = -delta * (1.0 - std::exp(-(r-r0)));
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

int main(int argc, char *argv[])
{
  const int num_steps = atoi(argv[1]);  //6000;
  const double dx = 0.4;
  const double dy = 0.4;
  const double dz = 0.4;
  const double dt = 0.01;

  const double r0 = 5.0;
  const double epsilon = 0.07;
  const double W0 = 1.0;
  const double beta0 = 0.0;
  const double D = 2.0;
  const double d0 = 0.5;
  const double a1 = 1.25 / std::sqrt(2.0);
  const double a2 = 0.64;
  const double lambda = (W0*a1)/(d0);
  const double tau0 = ((W0*W0*W0*a1*a2)/(d0*D)) + ((W0*W0*beta0)/(d0));

  // overall data set sizes
  const int nx = DATAXSIZE;
  const int ny = DATAYSIZE;
  const int nz = DATAZSIZE;
  const int vol = nx * ny * nz;
  const size_t vol_in_bytes = sizeof(double) * vol;

  // pointers for data set storage via malloc
  nRarray *phi_host;
  nRarray *d_phiold;
  nRarray *u_host;
  nRarray *d_phinew;
  nRarray *d_uold;
  nRarray *d_unew;
  nRarray *d_Fx;
  nRarray *d_Fy;
  nRarray *d_Fz;

The kernel thermalEquation operates on interior points where ix in [1,398], iy in [1,398], iz in [1,398], giving 398^3 = 63,044,792 active threads. For each active thread, the computation is:

1. Laplacian(uold, dx, dy, dz, ix, iy, iz):
   - phixx: uold[x+1][y][z] + uold[x-1][y][z] = 1 add; - 2.0*uold[x][y][z] = 1 mul + 1 sub; total so far = 1 add + 1 mul + 1 sub = 3 ops; then / SQ(dx) where SQ(dx) = dx*dx = 1 mul, then division = 1 div. So phixx = 3 + 1 + 1 = 5 ops.
   - phiyy: same structure = 5 ops.
   - phizz: same structure = 5 ops.
   - return phixx + phiyy + phizz = 2 adds.
   Total Laplacian = 17 ops.

2. Main expression:
   - 0.5*(phinew[ix][iy][iz] - phiold[ix][iy][iz]) = 1 sub + 1 mul = 2 ops.
   - dt * D * Laplacian(...): dt*D = 1 mul, then * result = 1 mul = 2 ops.
   - uold[ix][iy][iz] + term1 + term2 = 2 adds.
   Total main = 6 ops.

Total per active thread = 17 + 6 = 23 FP64 ops.

However, the compiler may precompute 1/SQ(dx), 1/SQ(dy), 1/SQ(dz) and use multiplications instead of divisions, and may fold dt*D into a single constant. Also, 2.0*phi[x][y][z] might be computed once and reused for all three terms. Let me count more carefully from the source:

- phi[x+1][y][z] + phi[x-1][y][z]: 1 FADD
- 2.0 * phi[x][y][z]: 1 FMUL
- subtract: 1 FADD (sub)
- / SQ(dx): SQ(dx) is a constant (0.16), so this is 1 FMUL (by reciprocal)
That's 4 ops for phixx. Same for phiyy (4) and phizz (4). But 2.0*phi[x][y][z] is the same for all three, so compiler may compute it once: saving 2 FMULs. So Laplacian = 4+4+4 - 2 + 2 (final adds) = 12. But let's be conservative and not assume CSE: 4*3 + 2 = 14 ops.

phiyy: add, mul, sub, mul = 4
phizz: add, mul, sub, mul = 4
phixx + phiyy: 1 add
+ phizz: 1 add
Laplacian total = 14

phinew - phiold: 1 sub
0.5 * diff: 1 mul
dt*D*Laplacian: dt*D is constant, so 1 mul
uold + 0.5*diff + dt*D*Lap: 2 adds
Total main = 5

prediction.fp32_flop_explanation: The kernel is entirely double precision in source and SASS except for a single compiler-generated `HFMA2.MMA ... 0,0` used for register materialization, which executes once per active thread. prediction.gridSz_explanation: From host code, the kernel launch uses dim3 grid((DATAZSIZE+7)/8, (DATAYSIZE+7)/8, (DATAXSIZE+3)/4) with DATAXSIZE=DATAYSIZE=DATAZSIZE=400. Thus the first thermalEquation invocation launches grid=(50,50,100).
prediction.blockSz_explanation: From host code, the shared block configuration for all kernels is dim3 block(8,8,4). The first thermalEquation invocation therefore uses block=(8,8,4), i.e. 256 threads per block.
prediction.fp32_flop_explanation: The kernel and all called device helpers operate on double-precision values only; there are no float or half variables or arithmetic in the executed path. Therefore FP32 work is zero for the first invocation.
prediction.fp64_flop_explanation: thermalEquation executes only for interior points 1..398 in each dimension, so 398^3 = 63,044,792 active threads. Per active thread: main update does 1 subtraction (phinew-phiold), 1 multiply by 0.5, 1 add to uold term, plus dt*D*Laplacian gives 1 multiply for dt*D, 1 multiply with Laplacian, and 1 final add = 6 FLOPs outside Laplacian; Laplacian itself computes three second-derivative terms, each as neighbor+neighbor (1 add), minus 2.0*center (1 mul + 1 sub), divided by SQ(d?) where SQ contributes 1 mul and the division 1 div, totaling 5 FLOPs per axis, plus two adds to sum phixx+phiyy+phizz, for 17 FLOPs. Total is 23 FP64 FLOPs per active thread, giving 63,044,792 * 23 = 1,450,030,216 FP64 FLOPs; boundary threads do no floating-point work because the if-body is skipped.
prediction.fp16_flop_explanation: The source contains no half-precision data or arithmetic, and there is no evidence of packed FP16 helper computation for this simple double-precision stencil kernel. Thus FP16 work is estimated as zero.
prediction.dram_bytes_read_explanation: The launch creates 50*50*100 blocks * 256 threads = 64,000,000 threads, but only the 398^3 interior threads read data. Each active thread reads 7 doubles from uold in Laplacian (center plus 6 neighbors), 1 double from uold for the explicit uold term, and 1 each from phinew and phiold, for 10 double reads = 80 bytes/thread; the unique read footprint across uold, phinew, phiold is about 3 arrays * 400^3 * 8 B = 1.536 GB, far larger than the 5 MB L2, so cache cannot retain the working set globally and a streaming estimate is appropriate. Therefore DRAM read bytes are estimated as 63,044,792 * 80 = 5,043,583,360 bytes for the first invocation.
prediction.dram_bytes_written_explanation: Only active interior threads write, each storing one double to unew, so source-level stores are 63,044,792 * 8 = 504,358,336 bytes. The written footprint for unew interior points alone is about 504 MB, much larger than the 5 MB L2, so these dirty cache lines will be evicted during the kernel and the first-invocation DRAM write traffic is approximated by the store footprint itself.

prediction.fp64_flop_explanation: The kernel applies boundary conditions by writing -delta to boundary elements. The DADD instruction computes -delta as DADD R, -RZ, -c[0x0][0x168], which is 1 FP64 operation per thread that hits a boundary condition. Every thread that passes the bounds check (iz < 400, iy < 400, ix < 400) enters the if-else chain. The total valid threads = 400*400*400 = 64,000,000. Each valid thread executes exactly one DADD (negation of delta) on exactly one taken branch path, regardless of whether it's a boundary or interior thread. Interior threads (those where ix, iy, iz are all not 0 and not 399) don't hit any branch and exit without a DADD — but actually looking at the code, interior threads don't write anything and just return. But actually, the launched grid is 50*8=400, 50*8=400, 100*4=400, so exactly 400^3 threads are launched, all pass bounds check. Each boundary thread executes exactly one DADD. So total FP64 FLOPs = 955,208. But wait — looking at SASS more carefully, the DADD is on every taken branch path. Interior threads that don't match any condition simply EXIT without executing DADD. So FP64 count = 955,208.
prediction.fp16_flop_explanation: There are two HFMA2.MMA instructions in the SASS (at 0x00e0 and 0x0160). The first at 0x00e0 is executed by all threads that pass the bounds check (64,000,000 threads). The second at 0x0160 is executed only by threads that don't match ix==0 and don't match ix==399, and need to compute a different address stride — these are threads with 0 < ix < 399 (i.e., ix in 1..398), so 398*400*400 = 63,680,000 threads. Total FP16 = 64,000,000 * 4 + 63,680,000 * 4 = 256,000,000 + 254,720,000 = 510,720,000.

prediction.fp64_flop_explanation:
The thermalEquation kernel operates on interior points where ix in [1,398], iy in [1,398], iz in [1,398], giving 398^3 = 63,044,792 active threads. For each active thread, the computation is:

1. Laplacian(uold, dx, dy, dz, ix, iy, iz):
   - phixx: uold[x+1][y][z] + uold[x-1][y][z] = 1 add; - 2.0*uold[x][y][z] = 1 mul + 1 sub; then /SQ(dx) where SQ(dx) is dx*dx = 1 mul, then division = 1 div. That's 4 ops per dimension.
   Actually let me count more carefully:
   - phixx = (phi[x+1][y][z] + phi[x-1][y][z] - 2.0 * phi[x][y][z]) / SQ(dx)
     - SQ(dx) = dx*dx: 1 mul
     - 2.0 * phi[x][y][z]: 1 mul
     - phi[x+1] + phi[x-1]: 1 add
     - result - 2.0*phi: 1 sub
     - / SQ(dx): 1 div
     Total: 5 ops
   - phiyy: same = 5 ops (but SQ(dy) could be reused; however counting source-level ops): 5 ops
   - phizz: same = 5 ops
   - phixx + phiyy: 1 add
   - + phizz: 1 add
   Laplacian total: 17 ops

2. Main expression:
   - 0.5*(phinew[ix][iy][iz] - phiold[ix][iy][iz]): 1 sub + 1 mul = 2 ops
   - dt * D: 1 mul
   - dt * D * Laplacian: 1 mul
   - uold[ix][iy][iz] + 0.5*(...): 1 add
   - + dt*D*Laplacian: 1 add
   Total main: 5 ops

Total per active thread: 17 + 5 = 22 FP64 ops.

However, the compiler may optimize SQ(dx), SQ(dy), SQ(dz) as constants since dx, dy, dz are kernel parameters passed as constants. The divisions by SQ(dx) etc. may be converted to multiply by reciprocal. Still counting as 1 op each.

Total FP64 = 22 * 63,044,792 = 1,386,985,424.

Note: Boundary threads (where the condition is false) do nothing, so 0 FP64 ops for them.

The kernel maps `blockIdx.x/y/z` to z/y/x respectively, but that only changes coordinate interpretation, not the launched grid dimensions.
prediction.blockSz_explanation: From host code, `block` is explicitly set to `dim3(8,8,4)` and passed unchanged to the first `allenCahn<<<grid, block>>>` launch. The SASS also confirms per-dimension block size values are read from launch constants and used with thread IDs in x/y/z.
prediction.fp32_flop_explanation: The kernel is entirely double-precision in source and SASS; there is no user-visible FP32 arithmetic on the main path. The only visible FP32 instructions in SASS are predicate/auxiliary operations and one packed HFMA2 constant-materialization instruction, so I conservatively attribute no FP32 FLOPs to this kernel.
prediction.fp64_flop_explanation: Only interior threads execute past the initial guard: indices 1..398 in each dimension, so 398^3 = 63,044,792 active threads. This excludes the out-of-line double-division helper because the denominators are compile-time normal constants and the branch to the helper is not taken on the observed path in SASS for these values.
prediction.fp16_flop_explanation: SASS shows one executed `HFMA2.MMA` instruction per active thread at 0x06f0, used for packed half-precision constant materialization. Per the instructions, compiler-generated packed FP16 arithmetic that executes must be counted; one HFMA2 contributes 4 FP16 FLOPs.
prediction.dram_bytes_read_explanation: The first invocation reads from five input arrays on the active path: 7 `phiold` values (center plus ±x, ±y, ±z), 6 force-neighbor values (Fx x-neighbors, Fy y-neighbors, Fz z-neighbors), and 1 `uold` center value, for 14 double loads = 112 bytes per interior thread. With 63,044,792 active threads that is 7,061,016,704 bytes of read traffic; the unique footprint touched across `phiold`, `uold`, `Fx`, `Fy`, and `Fz` is roughly 5 full 400^3 arrays ≈ 2.56 GB, far larger than A100 L2 (40 MB), so cache cannot retain the working set and DRAM reads are well approximated by the executed load traffic.
prediction.dram_bytes_written_explanation: Only interior threads write, with one `STG.E.64` to `phinew[ix][iy][iz]` per active thread, so total store traffic is 63,044,792 × 8 = 504,358,336 bytes. The written region is the interior of one 400^3 double array (~504 MB), far larger than 40 MB L2, so these dirty lines will be evicted during the kernel and the store traffic is a good estimate of DRAM bytes written during the first invocation.

records.kernel_demangled_name: calculateForce(double (*)[400][400], double (*)[400][400], double (*)[400][400], double (*)[400][400], double, double, double, double, double, double)

prediction.blockSz_explanation: From the host code: block = dim3(8, 8, 4). So blockSz = [8, 8, 4].
prediction.fp32_flop_explanation: No single-precision floating point operations are performed in this kernel; all arithmetic is double-precision (FP64).
prediction.fp64_flop_explanation:
Total threads launched = 50*50*100 * 8*8*4 = 250,000 * 256 = 64,000,000. The grid covers 400x400x400 = 64M threads exactly. Interior threads have ix in [1,398], iy in [1,398], iz in [1,398], so 398^3 = 63,044,792 interior threads. Boundary threads = 64,000,000 - 63,044,792 = 955,208.

For boundary threads (else branch): 0 FP64 ops (just storing 0.0 constants).

For each interior thread, the kernel computes:
- GradientX: sub + div = 2 ops (phi[x+1][y][z] - phi[x-1][y][z]) / (2.0*dx). The 2.0*dx is a constant that the compiler will precompute, so it's 1 sub + 1 div = 2 ops.
- GradientY: similarly 2 ops.
- GradientZ: similarly 2 ops.
- sqGphi = SQ(phix) + SQ(phiy) + SQ(phiz): 3 muls + 2 adds = 5 ops.
- c = 16.0 * W0 * epsilon: constant, precomputed on host, 0 ops at runtime.
- Wn calls An: An computes (assuming non-zero gradient for most interior threads):
  - (1.0 - 3.0*epsilon): constant = 0 ops
  - SQ(phix) = phix*phix: 1 mul (but already computed for sqGphi, compiler may reuse)
  - SQ(phix)*SQ(phix): phix^4, 1 mul (using phix^2)
  - Similarly phiy^4: 1 mul, phiz^4: 1 mul
  - Sum of 4th powers: phix^4 + phiy^4 + phiz^4: 2 adds
  - SQ(phix)+SQ(phiy)+SQ(phiz) = sqGphi (reused): 0 ops
  - sqGphi * sqGphi: 1 mul
  - ratio = sum4th / sqGphi^2: 1 div
  - 4.0*epsilon/(1.0-3.0*epsilon): constant = 0 ops
  - multiply by ratio: 1 mul
  - 1.0 + result: 1 add
  - multiply by (1.0-3.0*epsilon): 1 mul
  An total: ~3 muls for 4th powers + 2 adds + 1 mul (sqGphi^2) + 1 div + 1 mul + 1 add + 1 mul = 6 muls + 3 adds + 1 div = 10 ops
- w = W0 * An: 1 mul (W0=1.0 but compiler may not optimize away)
- w2 = w*w: 1 mul

For Fx: w2*phix: 1 mul; sqGphi*w: 1 mul; *c: 1 mul; dFunc(phix,phiy,phiz):
  dFunc: l=phix, m=phiy, n=phiz (non-zero case):
  - SQ(m)+SQ(n): 2 muls + 1 add (but SQ values reused from sqGphi)

The arrays involved are far larger than the 5 MB L2 (each 400^3 double field is 512 MB), so reuse is negligible at the DRAM level for this streaming first invocation; boundary threads perform no reads, yielding 63,044,792 * 120 = 7,565,375,040 bytes read.
args.dram_bytes_written_explanation: Only active interior threads write `phinew[ix][iy][iz]`, one double each, while out-of-bounds/boundary threads have no else-branch store in `allenCahn`. The written footprint is 398^3 doubles = 504,358,336 bytes, vastly exceeding the 5 MB L2, so these dirty lines will be evicted during the kernel and the first-invocation DRAM write estimate is the full output footprint.

prediction.fp32_flop_explanation: Looking at the SASS, there are FFMA instructions used as part of the FP64 division refinement checks (e.g., "FFMA R0, RZ, R7, R43" which is effectively a MOV but counts as an FP32 FMA = 2 FP32 FLOPs). These appear in the three gradient divisions (for phix, phiy, phiz) and in the An() computation divisions (up to 3 more divisions for An and dFunc calls). For interior threads (398^3 = 63,044,792), each executes the taken path with these FFMA instructions. There are approximately 6 FFMA instructions on the main fast path for interior threads (one per division attempt: 3 for gradients, 1 for An's inner division of 4ε/(1-3ε) by the squared sum, 1 for An's outer division of (phix^4+phiy^4+phiz^4)/(sum^2), and up to 3 for the three dFunc calls). However, most interior threads have phi=±1 uniformly, so gradients are zero for most threads, hitting the else branch (P0=false). Let me reconsider: the initial phi is a sphere of radius 5 in a 400^3 grid, so only a thin shell of threads near the sphere boundary will have non-zero gradients. For the vast majority of interior threads, phix=phiy=phiz=0, so they take the !P0 branch at 0x7f0. For those threads, the FFMA count from the gradient divisions is 3 (one per gradient: phix, phiy, phiz divisions each have one FFMA for the fast-path check). For the An computation when all gradients are zero, the !P0 branch at 0x7f0 is taken (no division FFMA). For dFunc when all zero, the branches skip the division FFMAs. So for most threads: 3 FFMAs from gradient divisions = 6 FP32 FLOPs each. For boundary threads (total threads - interior = 250000*256 - 63044792 = 955208 boundary threads that write zeros), they don't execute FFMAs. Total threads = 50*50*100*8*8*4 = 64,000,000. Interior threads = 398^3 = 63,044,792. Of these, most have zero gradients. The 3 FFMA instructions execute for all interior threads regardless (they're on the fast path before the branch). Each FFMA = 2 FP32 FLOPs. So ~63,044,792 * 3 * 2 = 378,268,752. But actually looking more carefully at the SASS, the FFMA at 0x340 is "FFMA R0, RZ, R7, R43" which computes 0*R7+R43 = R43, effectively a move but still an FP32 FLOP (2 ops: mul+add). Similarly at 0x4f0, 0x6a0. These 3 FFMAs execute for all interior threads. Then for threads with zero gradients, the !P0 path at 0x7f0 has a DFMA but no FFMA. The dFunc paths also skip when zero. So total FP32 = 63,044,792 * 3 * 2 = 378,268,752.
prediction.fp64_flop_explanation:
Let me analyze the FP64 operations per thread. Total launched threads = 50*50*100*256 = 64,000,000. Boundary threads (ix=0 or 399, iy=0 or 399, iz=0 or 399, or any index ≥400 due to grid rounding — but grid is exactly 400 in each dim so no excess): boundary threads that fail the interior check = 64,000,000 - 398^3 = 955,208. These just store zeros (no FP64 ops).

For interior threads (63,044,792): Most have phi uniformly ±1 (sphere of radius 5 centered at (200,200,200)). For threads far from the sphere boundary, phi[x+1]=phi[x-1]=phi[x]=same value, so gradients = 0.

For each interior thread, the gradient computations involve:
- GradientX: DADD (subtract) + division by 2*dx. The division is computed via Newton-Raphson: DADD(2*dx), MUFU.RCP64H, 5 DFMA, 1 DMUL, then refinement DFMA+DFMA = total ~10 FP64 ops for the division. Looking at SASS 0x280-0x340: DADD(1), MUFU.RCP64H(1 counted as FP64), DFMA×5, DMUL×1, DADD(subtraction of phi values at 0x2f0) = DADD(1) + MUFU(1) + 5 DFMA(10) + DMUL(2) + DADD(2 for the phi subtraction) = but let me count more carefully from SASS.

For phix (0x220-0x340): LDG×2, then DADD R6 (=2*dx, 1 op), MUFU.RCP64H (1 op), DFMA×5 (10 ops), DADD R4 (phi subtraction, 1 op but it's -R4+R2 = 1 op), DMUL R42 (2 ops), DFMA (2 ops), DFMA (2 ops) = 1+1+10+1+2+2+2 = 19 FP64 ops per gradient. Similarly for phiy and phiz = 19 each, total 57.

For threads with zero gradients (phix=phiy=phiz=0), the !P0 branch at 0x7f0:
- DMUL R34 (phix²), DMUL R32 (phiy²), DMUL R22 (phiz²) = 6 ops (these execute before the branch)
- DSETP tests (not counted as FLOPs)
- !P0 path: DFMA R4 = epsilon * (-5/3) + 1 = 2 ops. Plus loading constants.
Total for zero-gradient: 57 (gradients) + 6 (squares) + 2 (An else branch) = 65 FP64 ops.

Then for Fx/Fy/Fz computation when gradients=0: sqGphi=0, w=An*W0, w2=w², but the stores are w2*0 + 0*w*c*0 = 0. Looking at SASS after 0xb80:
- DADD R6 (R34+R32, 1 op), DMUL R4 (An*W0, 2 ops), DMUL R2 (16*W0*epsilon chain: 2+2+2=6 ops from 0xc20-0xc40), DADD R6 (R22+R6, 1 op), DMUL R16 (2 ops), DMUL R16 (2 ops), DMUL R18 (w², 2 ops).
For dFunc with zero args: branches skip to store zeros.
- DFMA R4 (R18*phix + ..., 2 ops) for Fx, similarly for Fy and Fz.
- DMUL R36 (2 ops), DFMA R36 (2 ops) for Fy.
- DMUL R4 (2 ops), DFMA R4 (2 ops) for Fz.

Counting post-An for zero-gradient threads: DADD(1) + DMUL(2) + DMUL(2) + DMUL(2) + DADD(1) + DMUL(2) + DMUL(2) + DMUL(2) + DMUL(2) + DFMA(2) + DMUL(2) + DFMA(2) + DMUL(2) + DFMA(2) = ~26 FP64 ops.

Total per zero-gradient interior thread: 57 + 6 + 2 + 26 = 91 FP64 ops.

For the ~63M interior threads, the vast majority have zero gradients. The sphere surface threads (radius 5, ~4π*25 ≈ 314 surface cells, but in 3D grid it's a thin shell, maybe ~2000 threads) have non-zero gradients with many more FP64 ops (An taken path + dFunc divisions). This is negligible compared to 63M.

Approximate total FP64 = 63,044,792 * 91 ≈ 5,737,076,072. The boundary threads contribute 0 FP64 ops.
prediction.fp16_flop_explanation: No FP16 operations are present in this kernel. The SASS shows no HADD2, HFMA2, or other FP16 instructions.
prediction.dram_bytes_read_explanation: Each interior thread reads 6 doubles from phi array (phi[x+1][y][z], phi[x-1][y][z], phi[x][y+1][z], phi[x][y-1][z], phi[x][y][z+1], phi[x][y][z-1]) = 6 LDG.E.64 instructions. The phi array is 400×400×400×8 = 512,000,000 bytes. The unique read footprint is essentially the entire phi array (since interior threads touch all elements except corners that are only read by boundary-adjacent threads). The L2 cache is 6 MB = 6,291,456 bytes, which is much smaller than 512 MB, so most reads will miss in L2 and go to DRAM. The total load traffic is 63,044,792 × 6 × 8 = 3,026,150,016 bytes, but with cache line reuse (each 128-byte cache line holds 16 doubles, and neighboring threads in z-dimension share cache lines), the actual DRAM read traffic is closer to the unique footprint. The unique footprint of phi is ~512 MB (all elements are touched by some thread). With streaming access patterns and 6 MB L2, DRAM reads ≈ 512,000,000 bytes for the unique phi footprint. However, the access pattern has 6 different offsets per thread, causing cache thrashing for the large working set. The effective DRAM reads are approximately the unique footprint: ~512,000,000 bytes.
prediction.dram_bytes_written_explanation: Each thread writes to Fx, Fy, and Fz arrays (3 STG.E.64 instructions per thread = 24 bytes per thread). Total threads = 64,000,000 (all threads write, including boundary threads that write 0.0). Total unique write footprint = 3 arrays × 400×400×400 × 8 bytes = 1,536,000,000 bytes. The L2 cache is only 6 MB, so the vast majority of written cache lines will be evicted to DRAM during the kernel execution. DRAM bytes written ≈ 1,536,000,000 bytes.
